correctness.rationale: For alpha>-1 the normalized radial beta integral gives norm squared 1/c_j for z^j. The polygon DFT isolates one orthogonal vector per residue modulo m; the squared e_N-coordinate of the matching normalized vector is exactly the stated probability. At s=e^(-t/N) its log derivative is the tilted mean of j/N minus one, with derivative minus the strictly positive variance. As t decreases to zero, the partition sum diverges and the tilted mass leaves each fixed initial index block, so the mean tends to infinity. At large t the smallest index dominates. These facts prove the two radius claims, including nonattainment for m>N. For varying m/N tending to zero, the scaled coefficients c_j/N^(beta-1) are bounded by a constant times ((j+1)/N)^(beta-1); truncation near zero and at infinity together with the shifted mesh m/N proves the gamma Riemann-sum limit, locally uniformly in t also for the first tilted moment. The log derivative brackets the global optimizer on either side of beta. At a positive limit c<1, index j=N+km gives the claimed lattice series by dominated convergence, also for its first moment: if 1+kc=0, admissible j=o(N) contributes zero in the limit by the same coefficient bound. For the limiting lattice, mass escapes to infinity as t decreases to zero and at large t concentrates on a point below one; the negative-variance derivative gives uniqueness and the same sign bracket controls the finite optimizers. Near m/N=1 from below or at equality only j=N-m is below N. Writing a=c_(N-m)/c_N and b=c_(N+m)/c_N, the two nearest relative contributions have sum at least 2 sqrt(ab), with equality at exp(-tm/N)=sqrt(a/b); the remaining geometric-polynomial tail at this test point is O(a). Inverting the minimized denominator gives the deficit equivalence, valid even for bounded N-m, since a tends to zero and b tends to 2^(beta-1).
residual_risks: The supplied 630-count marker is diagnostic: some critical test cases increment a counter even if the accuracy assertion is skipped, and the script does not certify the lattice limit. The proof, not the finite tests, establishes all regimes. No unconstrained optimality is claimed.

value.rationale: Regular equally spaced kernels are a canonical symmetric dictionary. For growing target degree, knowing separately that sublinear sampling captures a vanishing fraction, linear sampling captures a strictly intermediate lattice-controlled fraction, and nearly degree-many nodes capture almost everything with a sharp square-root deficit is useful for choosing both sample count and radius. The critical formula distinguishes bounded from growing N-m and quantifies saturation before the exact m>N transition. These simultaneous limits answer a real optimization question beyond the already covered finite identity and fixed-m Gamma law.
residual_risks: The utility is within the symmetric dictionary; the result does not decide whether an arbitrary node set needs this many kernels.
